articles.title: Lobos position preview: DE Darren Agu giving Lobo defensive line a 'Freaks List' worthy presence
articles.summary: Last summer, Darren Agu had to make do with two trees for practice partners — one to practice his pass rush moves and the other to actually strike. “People w...
articles.body:
Last summer, Darren Agu had to make do with two trees for practice partners — one to practice his pass rush moves and the other to actually strike.

"People would walk by and look at me like, 'yo, what the heck? He's striking a tree,'" New Mexico's fifth-year defensive end laughed. "Leaves (were) falling down the tree, fruit, bugs. I'm like, 'you gotta get the strikes in somehow.'"

With a full offseason under his belt — one he was denied last summer — Agu believes he's playing at a "higher level" than he was in his first year with UNM.

In his first season with the Lobos, the former Vanderbilt transfer posted 15 total tackles, two sacks and 26 pressures, the third-best mark on the team. Agu, however, had to play catch-up for the entire year after visa issues kept him in his native London over the summer, holding him out of workouts and fall camp.

Before he made it back to Albuquerque in early September, Agu did his best with the equipment he had. He lifted and ran in accordance with the Lobos' offseason conditioning program. He watched the program's season opener against Michigan via FaceTime.

And in a public park, he found those two trees.

One passerby saw the towering 6-foot-6, 256-pound defensive end slamming his hands into the bark and stopped to ask if he was a rugby player.

"My forearms (and) my palms would be swollen, hitting the tree and stuff," Agu said. "But I was getting that work in, though."

This summer, Agu is reaping the benefits of a proper offseason. Off the field, he was named to the "Freaks List," an annual ranking of the freakiest athletes in college football by The Athletic's Bruce Feldman.

The list claims Agu benched 385 pounds and ran a 10-yard split in 1.61 seconds this offseason, a mix of power and speed that seems to be impress everybody but him.

"In the weight room, we do lifts and stuff and there would be times when I'd throw up a number," Agu said, "and (director of athletic performance Caleb Heim) and some of the strength coaches would be like, 'oh s***!' So I'd be like, 'is that crazy or something?'"

On the field? Agu is set to replace All-Mountain West defensive end Keyshawn James-Newby as UNM's starting Jack (boundary end) with a more pronounced presence as a pass rusher than last season.

Already a stout run defender, Agu has worked to become a more effective rusher through film study and walkthroughs.

"In the pass rush aspect, he's doing so much better (at feeling) and seeing what he's getting, and reacting to it," defensive line coach Hebron Fangupo said.

With fifth-year defensive end Brett Karhu currently ineligible, College of San Mateo transfer Albert Tuakalau is expected to start opposite of Agu. The 6-4, 245-pound junior flashed heavily this spring before cementing himself as one of UNM's top three defensive ends in camp.

Memphis transfer Jalen Charles, Copiah-Lincoln (Mississippi) Community College transfer Trenton Rocker and West Mesa graduate Elijah Brody are expected to provide further depth off the edge.

"He brings the Albuquerque grit and toughness," Fangupo said of Brody. "That's what gives him value. He's plenty athletic, he's got his speed, but man, he's a tough kid – if he had a choice, he'll run through your face."

On the interior, UNM will rely on defensive tackles Brian Booker, Jalen McIver and Xavier Slayton, who all logged 200-plus snaps last season. A preseason All-Mountain West selection, Booker said earlier this summer that he's looking to make more plays after leaving "a lot of meat on the table" last season.

Fangupo said he's proud of the 6-3, 325-pound fifth-year senior for his continued growth.

"He's gotten so much better in the mental aspect – being in control of what he can control and executing at a high level, penetrating low, fast and aggressive," he added. "But better yet, he's challenging his brothers to do the same … He's (running and finishing plays) more in practice and when he does that, we're so good, because he knows everything starts with the nose tackle."

Independence (Kansas) Community College transfer A.J. Robinson, sophomore Jake DeVos and Western New Mexico transfer – a La Cueva graduate and the older brother of Arizona State quarterback Cam Dyer – have helped provide depth on the interior.

"With Jalen and (Booker), we got some power out there … (Robinson and DeVos), they bring a different speed and agility to our play," Fangupo said. "And that's what we love about them – they are relentless, they play hard, play fast. But we gotta continue to bring them along."

Sean Reider covers college football and other sports for the Journal. You can reach him at sreider@abqjournal.com or via X at @lenaweereider.

articles.title: Duran’s Slam and Mickey’s Magic power the Red Sox to 7-3 extra-innings win in Miami
articles.summary: “I felt like a 100 pound weight was lifted off my shoulders.” — Jarren Duran after his tenth inning grand slam.
articles.body:
That's how Dan Secatore began the game recap here at Over The Monster after Saturday's heart-pounding win at Fenway . But you know what? That's becoming an increasingly appropriate way to start off every game recap around here.

Make no mistake, the Red Sox should have lost this game. They should have lost it when they gave the Marlins 14 at bats with runners in scoring position. They should have lost it when Payton Tolle ran out of gas at the end of his outing and allowed five of the last eight men he faced to reach base (including a Heriberto Hernandez home run). And they especially should have lost it in the bottom of the tenth when Aroldis Chapman wasn't available to close out a one run game and both Andruw Monasterio and Connor Wong made critical blunders that forced the bottom of the bullpen to get five outs in the inning.

Wong's egregious effort was specifically problematic because it should have ended the game. Wyatt Olds pitched his butt off and nearly got the equivalent of a four out save (I'm counting Monasterio's throwing error to lead off the inning as one of them), but because Wong couldn't move his butt on what should have been the final pitch of the evening, the ball went to the backstop and the Red Sox needed another inning to win the game.

Very, very rarely does a team recover from a play like this:

But this is the summer of 2026, and like a law of the universe that doesn't fully make sense, the Red Sox find inexplicable ways to win.

So of course, the Marlins go just 1-14 with the chances they had with men in scoring position. And of course, the leadoff double Payton Tolle gives up when he's teetering gets thrown out at third on the next play. And of course the Red Sox still manage to escape the tenth inning with Alec Gamboa on the mound. And of course they immediately follow that up with Jarren Duran grand slam in the 11th after he was hitless all night.

Here's the shot from Duran that proved to be the knockout blow:

But that wasn't even all of the magic, because before the game ever reached extras, the Sox were getting more incredible production from an unlikely source.

Normally when you're looking for Mickey Magic in Florida, you go to Orlando. Tonight, the Red Sox got it in Miami. Mickey Gasper went deep twice, and both to a deep part of the ballpark. Here's the first bomb:

You know what's crazy? Those Gasper home runs landed a little to each side of where Roman Anthony 's home run in the World Baseball Classic that proved to be the game winner against the Dominican Republic landed.

Speaking of Roman Anthony home runs, he was doing this in Worcester while all that was going on in Miami:

And while Andruw Monasterio was throwing the ball away in the tenth, Trevor Story was striking out on pitches like this:

I can't ever remember a night where two games at the MLB and Triple-A level were working in tandem to make a gaggle of upcoming roster crunch decisions more and more complex. This is wild stuff. What a night, what a team, what a summer!

Jarren Duran: Went straight from the dud pile (being 0-4 through ten innings) to the top of the stud mountain with his game winning grand slam.

Mickey Gasper: This guy had zero career home runs in a Red Sox uniform eight days ago. He now has five.

Erik Miller : Looked outstanding again as he struck out the side in the ninth. He still hasn't give up an earned run in the Red Sox uniform.

Wyatt Olds: Very rarely do we hand out studs to the guy who gets tagged with a blown save, but Olds deserved better as he essentially got four outs and was kneecapped by Monasterio and Wong. Over The Monster's own Jacob Roy will have more on Olds's inning tomorrow, so be on the lookout for that.

Andruw Monasterio: 1-5 at the plate, and the nearly crippling error in the bottom of the tenth. He did recover and field the final out however. (Now we await roster decisions to see if this was his final game of the 2026 season at the major league level.)

Connor Wong: He has to get in front of that ball in the bottom of the tenth. That's the type of play that makes me want Mickey Gasper as the backup catcher to Rutschman with Wong in Worcester.

Payton Tolle: As great as he looked early on, he was coming unglued at the end of the outing, and this is also kind of a big picture problem in the macro of the season. He's been better on longer rest all year, so how much does he have in the tank for late September and October? Navigating his usage will be incredibly tricky over the next few weeks (and hopefully next two months).

Duran's grand slam. So nice, it's worth seeing twice.

articles.title: Jays Lose Another Frustrating Game
articles.summary: Royals 5 Blue Jays 3 Well, that was a frustrating game. As I said in the thread, we weren’t going to run the table. If they had to win every game left to get...
articles.body:
As I said in the thread, we weren't going to run the table. If they had to win every game left to get into the playoffs, it wasn't going to happen. They need to win most of their games, but not all of them.

That ninth inning……After two outs, Daz Cameron singled. Brett Bateman followed with a single and went to second on defensive indifference. Nathan Lukes singled them both home.

And then…..Lukes ignored the first base coach's stop sign and was thrown out trying to turn it into a double. This CAN NOT HAPPEN . His run didn't matter. If he score from second on a single, we would still be behind. He had to stop at first and hope that Vlad has another good at bat. You can not get thrown out at second when you aren't the tying run. I don't know what he was thinking.

The eighth inning was pretty much the tale of the season:

An out later, Jesús Sanchez was hit by pitch. Bases loaded for

Ernie Clement who, ummmm, fouled a ball off a part of the male anatomy that you really don't want to foul a ball off. He was down for a while. I was of the opinion they should take him out of the game. I know I wouldn't be able to hit after that. But, he stayed in and popped one to medium center. In the top of the ninth he dived for a ball and stayed on the ground for a bit, you know he was still hurting. Hitting a baseball is tough, hitting a baseball after being hit in the nuts, is impossible.

We had those two runs in the ninth and one in the first. Bateman and Lukes started the game with singles. An out later, Kazuma Okamoto walked to load the bases. Jesús Sánchez hit a sac fly. Clements followed with a strikeout.

Andrés Giménez hit a double to lead off the second, but we couldn't get him past third.

In the fourth, Clement and Giménez had one-out singles and Brandon Valenuela hit into a double play.

In the fifth, Bateman had a one-out single and went to second on an error, but ground out (Lukes) and flyout (Vlad) ended that.

In the seventh, Andrés Giménez was hit by pitch to start the inning, but Kirk hit into a double play.

And, well, we talked about the eighth and ninth.

Max Scherzer had a rough first inning, loading the bases on two walks and single, before getting his first out, but even with another walk, he only allowed one run. And he gave up another in the fifth. A one-out walk and two two-out singles scored the run, but he got out of it from there.

Five innings, four hits, two earned, five walks and four strikeouts. Which, other than the walks, was about the best we could hope from Max.

Braydon Fisher also had a rough time of it in the sixth, giving up two hits and as it turned out, two runs. But they weren't earned.

Mason Fluharty came in and Kyle Isbel put down a sac bunt, the runner from third wasn't coming out. But Vlad picked up the ball half way down the first base line, turned and threw side arm, well wide of Clement at first. One run scored. Quick play, but you have to make a better throw. Preferably not side arm (sidearm throws tend to slide to the arm side). A sac fly scored the other run.

Paul Swwald gave up a hit and two walks, but no runs in the seventh.

Brandon Little walked one, but had three strikeouts, in the eighth.

Tyler Rogers went single, steal, strikeout, ground out (runner to third) and single, scoring the run. I often say that the trouble with ground ball pitchers is that sometimes the ground balls find holes (of course the trouble with fly ball pitchers is some fly balls clear the fence, safer to strikeout everyone out).

We had 10 hits. Bateman had 3. Lukes and Giménez two. Okamoto, Sánchez (with a hit batter and a sac fly), Valenzuela/Kirk and Straw all had 0 fors.

1 for 11 with RISP just isn't going to cut it.

Other Award: Well, Lukes for going for second and ending the game, gets one. And Valenzuale (-0.15, plus a poor challenge, he also had a good challenge), Clement (-0.12, and he'll never have children again), Kirk (-0.10), and Straw (-0.10, but did make a great catch in left).

Tomorrow we have a bullpen day. As Jamie says, we've done very well in bullpen days. Of course, my objection to bullpen days isn't the game itself, it is the strain on the bullpen arms. Randy Dobnak (2-1, 1.58 ERA, in 9 games, 7 starts).

articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Pitt strong safety Brandon Hill, the team announced on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed former Pitt strong safety Brandon Hill , the team announced on Tuesday.

Hill, 25, was a seventh-round pick of the Houston Texans in the 2023 NFL Draft and has bounced around the league from Houston to the Las Vegas Raiders and most recently, the Chicago Bears , who released him on Aug. 11.

A 5-foot-11, 195-pound native of Apopka, Florida, Hill redshirted in 2019, and became a regular in 2020 before starting in his final two seasons at Pitt in 2021 and 2022. He had three interceptions and nine passes defended over his Panthers career, including a pix six in 2020 against Florida State.

articles.title: 12-year-old hailed âheroâ for calling 911 before Montana gunman killed her, 7 others
articles.summary: US News: A 12-year-old girl called 911 from inside a Montana home as a gunman killed eight relatives, including four children, during a Sunday family dinner ou.
articles.body: A 12-year-old girl called 911 from inside a Montana home as a gunman killed eight relatives, including four children, during a Sunday family dinner outside Billings. The victims belonged to four generations of the same blended family.Charlotte Ghekiere, 12, was among those killed. Family friend Jennifer Mercer said the girl called 911 and tried to save her relatives, something the family wanted made public. âThe one thing we do know is that Charlotte was the hero,â Mercer said.The gunman was identified by relative Brad Ireland as Alan Smith, 44. Smith had lived with his parents for years before they asked him to leave a couple of weeks earlier, but he returned unexpectedly on Sunday evening as relatives gathered for their regular family dinner and opened fire, Ireland said, according to news agency Associated Press.Victims spanned four generationsThe oldest victim was Smithâs grandmother, Evelyn Smith, who was in her 90s, used a wheelchair and lived in a nearby retirement community. The youngest was 7-year-old Chloe Ireland.Smithâs parents, Dana and Barb Smith, and his younger sister, Megan Ghekiere, were also killed. Meganâs children with former husband Brad Ireland, Owen Ireland, 13, and Chloe, were among the four children who died.Her two stepchildren with current husband Adam Ghekiere, Landon Ghekiere, 15, and Charlotte, 12, were also killed. Mercer, who was authorized to release information about the victims, later launched an online appeal to help the family meet funeral and other expenses.She described the family as close and loving, saying the children got along and their parents remained amicable even after divorcing. She also said the deaths had devastated the wider community, including people who had never known the family.Officers heard shots before flames engulfed houseOfficers arrived at the property on Sunday evening and heard gunshots from the rear of the house. Soon afterwards, flames engulfed the building.Investigators confirmed on Tuesday that eight people had been killed, including four children. They also said the suspect had suffered a self-inflicted gunshot wound and later died. Ireland said Smith killed his grandmother, parents, younger sister and the four children before setting the house on fire. He added that Smith tried to flee before encountering law enforcement.Firefighters could not immediately tackle the blaze because authorities first had to secure the scene. Once they were able to enter the area, crews continued fighting the fire until about 1am on Monday, Billings Fire Department Chief Matt Hoppel said.The subdivision is outside Billings city limits and is not required to have fire hydrants. The delay in starting firefighting operations gave the flames additional time to spread through the house.Family moved to Montana from Seattle areaThe family originally came from the Seattle area. After Ireland and Megan divorced six years ago, she moved to Montana with their children, where she later met Adam Ghekiere, who became her second husband.Her parents, Dana and Barb Smith, subsequently followed her to Montana and settled in Billings nearby. Danaâs elderly mother, Evelyn, lived separately in a retirement community in the area, Ireland said.Alan Smith had also been living in Montana with his parents for several years before they recently asked him to leave. He returned to their home on Sunday evening while relatives were gathering for their regular family meal.Adam Ghekiere was at work and was not at the house when the shooting occurred.Relative says there were âmany red flagsâIreland, who lives in Arizona and lost his former wife and two children in the shooting, said there had been warning signs involving Smith.âThere were many red flags and many people spoke out,â he said. âNo one listened.âHe described Smith as a âhermitâ who generally remained in his room and spent much of his time on a computer. Ireland said relatives did not know what he did there throughout the day.Smith attended Eastern Washington University but had been unable to find a job or keep one. Criminal-record checks in Montana and Washington also found no previous arrest or criminal charge involving him.Ireland said he was unaware of any previous violence by Smith, although he said his former brother-in-law could be verbally abusive.Friends of the victims have since created two GoFundMe campaigns to support Adam Ghekiere and his former wife, Erica Schneider.Montana case is 22nd US mass killing this yearThe case is the 22nd US mass killing recorded this year by a database compiled by the news agency and USA Today with Northeastern University. Of those incidents, 15 stemmed from domestic disputes.James Alan Fox, the Northeastern University criminologist responsible for the database, said domestic disputes account for about half of US mass killings on average.No US mass killing since April has had a higher death toll. In that earlier Louisiana case, a father killed eight children, seven of them his own, and wounded his wife and another woman.Husband raced home after hearing shooting alertAdam Ghekiere was working at the Billings airport when he heard a report of an active shooting over a dispatch radio. He immediately called each member of his family before driving across Billings to the Smith home.By the time he arrived, the house was already ablaze. About two hours later, he learned that his wife and children had been killed.Ghekiere said he had not expected his children to be at the gathering because the family normally held its dinner on Fridays. Their presence that Sunday also led him to believe Smith had not expected to find them there.âI donât think he expected my kids to be there,â he said, referring to his brother-in-law.Police later told Ghekiere that Charlotte had made the emergency call from inside the house. As he recalled his daughter, he said one particular exchange continued to stay with him.âI keep hearing her quote to me every time I would say âI love youâ and she would say âI love you more,ââ he said.Fire damage complicates investigationThe fire burned the house to its foundation, leaving investigators with concerns about the structural integrity of what remained. articles.title: Trump will need China for his new economic war against Iran. Good luck getting Xi on side
articles.summary: Beijing has shown itself wary of playing a direct mediator role in the conflict, preferring a position where it protects its own economic interests – and plays up its image as a stable power that supports regional peace, in contrast to Washington’s vacillations.
articles.body: When US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast,” threatening damaging new sanctions on countries that refuse to stop doing business with Iran, he didn’t name the one country that could decide its success or failure: China. The world’s second-largest economy has long been a critical economic lifeline for Tehran, buying up the vast majority of its oil exports – worth an estimated tens of billions in US dollars last year – in addition to other trade. Bringing it on board with the White House’s latest effort to subdue an Iranian leadership stubbornly defiant after almost six months of war, however, is an extremely tall order. Beijing flatly rejects what it calls “unilateral” US sanctions and has long defended its right to regular trade with partners like Iran and Russia. It also surmises that Washington would be wary of triggering a broader economic confrontation that would hurt both countries, right ahead of the US midterms. On Tuesday, following Bessent’s press conference, China’s Foreign Ministry vowed to “take all necessary measures” to safeguard its “own legitimate rights and interests” in the face of US sanction threats. “Economic warfare and maximum pressure will not help resolve the issue; they will only further intensify tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order,” ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said. Bessent’s threat also comes ahead of a highly anticipated visit by Chinese leader Xi Jinping to the US next month, where the two sides could make progress on extending a critical trade truce set to expire later this fall. US President Donald Trump earlier said that he did not ask Xi “for any favors” on Iran during a May meeting between the two – a statement which, if correct, will likely smell to Beijing of American desperation to end the conflict. What’s left now is a careful calculus for both countries in how they navigate what Bessent has said will be a period of “quiet diplomacy” – or privately issuing ultimatums to Iran’s economic partners, which the Treasury chief did not specifically name during his press conference. Chinese analysts suggest limited space for Washington’s demands. “China is unlikely to accept a situation in which Washington determines what Chinese companies can legally trade with third countries,” said Zhao Long, director of the Institute for International Strategic and Security Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies. “That would establish a precedent that US secondary sanctions can effectively determine China’s commercial relations with third countries.” What Washington could do China imports Iranian oil using a shadowy system that’s by design insulated from the US dollar system – and sanctions. Private, so-called teapot refineries purchase and process US-sanctioned Iranian crude, relying on a network of ports, financial institutions and tankers that are often similarly firewalled from international exposure. China hasn’t recorded these purchases officially in years, since the US re-imposed sanctions on Iran when the first Trump administration backed out of the Obama-era Iranian nuclear deal. But pressure points do exist, analysts say. “When you look at the upstream ownership of these entities, you’ll find many are directly or indirectly held by major Chinese state-owned entities that are heavily integrated into the US dollar system,” said Max Meizlish, a senior research analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies think tank in Washington. “By sanctioning their subsidiaries, the US can apply pressure on the parents to divest at risk of being deemed as providing direct or indirect support to sanctioned entities,” he said. Bessent earlier this year said Washington has sent warnings to two unnamed Chinese banks about their role in Iran-linked transactions. When asked on Monday during his press conference what measures the US would take against non-compliant Chinese banks and shipping firms, he said “no one is above” facing US sanctions. Despite the tough talk, Beijing has seen the US threaten – and then back off from – sweeping sanctions before. And it also knows Washington is acutely aware of China’s significant economic leverage over the US, especially in the form of its grip on the global supply of strategically critical rare earths. “If Washington crossed that threshold (of sanctioning major Chinese banks), Beijing would almost certainly respond, and the political atmosphere for a summit (between Trump and Xi) would deteriorate sharply,” said Sun Chenghao, a senior fellow at Tsinghua University’s Center for International Security and Strategy in Beijing. Such a move might not automatically cancel their meeting, but it would “shift the summit from stabilization toward damage control,” he said. Summit considerations Both sides will be weighing up the impact of escalation on that summit, expected to be the first state visit by Xi to the US in 11 years. While Beijing will not want to be seen to be cooperating with a sanctions regime it opposes, there are careful maneuvers it could take – such as quietly reducing oil purchases or elevating its political messaging to Tehran and efforts to encourage restraint. Chinese purchases of Iranian oil have already declined sharply compared with last year as the US blockade has constrained Iranian crude exports. Chinese analysts have also in recent weeks suggested there are overlaps between the interests of Washington and Beijing, especially in terms of seeing trade flows restored in the Strait of Hormuz, which has been choked by the conflict, and restoring broader regional stability, also conductive to trade. And Beijing has in recent days re-upped its messaging urging restraint and normal operations around the strait. In a joint statement following a meeting with Jordanian King Abdullah II in Beijing on Monday, Xi called for the restoration of “normal passage” through the strait and a “comprehensive solution” to the conflict. Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Miao Deyu said last week while hosting Iranian officials in Beijing that China was “actively committed to promoting peace talks.” Even still, Beijing has shown itself wary of playing a direct mediator role in the conflict, preferring a position where it protects its own economic interests – and plays up its image as a stable power that supports regional peace, in contrast to Washington’s vacillations. Any cooperation with the US in restoring regional peace “should not be reduced to ‘doing Trump a favor,’” said Zhao in Shanghai. “Beijing is willing to contribute to ending the crisis, but it is not willing to become an instrument of Washington’s maximum-pressure strategy.”

articles.title: Why Tesla has been caught up in a massive car recall in China
articles.summary: The country's biggest ever car recall affects more than four million vehicles made by Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and other firms.
articles.body:
Hidden car door handles - the sleek designs often found on electric vehicles (EVs) - have come under the spotlight over the past week.

That's after China announced its biggest ever recall of cars, with more than four million vehicles - mostly Teslas - affected .

The recall comes ahead of new regulations in China , requiring cars to have a mechanical release both on the inside and outside of their doors.

Popularised by Elon Musk's electric vehicle giant, this type of handle has become commonplace around the world.

But several incidents have raised concerns that this design may make doors difficult to open in an emergency.

Hidden door handles are widely used in modern cars in China, with around 60% of the top 100 best-selling new energy vehicles, including EVs and hybrids, having them.

The minimalist design gives vehicles a "sleek look and reduces wind drag" but can be confusing to use, car industry analyst Stephen Dyer from consultancy AlixPartners told the BBC.

"Even I often find it difficult to locate the switch to open the door from the inside of an unfamiliar vehicle," said Dyer, who is based in Shanghai.

But beyond their usability, the handles have been blamed for endangering the lives of drivers and passengers.

Electronically powered door handles became an industry trend, but raised "real safety concerns" when doors failed to open promptly, delaying rescue efforts after accidents, said Nanyang Technological University associate professor Lyu Chen.

"A door handle may seem simple, but it becomes safety-critical in the seconds after a crash," Chen said.

Chinese carmaker Xiaomi faced intense scrutiny following two fatal crashes in 2025 involving its SU7 model, when suspected electrical failures allegedly trapped occupants.

One of the incidents took place on a highway in Tongling city, eastern China, killing three people, according to regional news coverage cited by state-controlled media Global Times.

Relatives of the victims said the passengers were stuck in the car as the vehicle's doors could not be unlocked after the collision, the outlet said.

At the time, Xiaomi's representatives said the SU7 had mechanical emergency release handles that function even without power, which are located at the bottom of each door.

The company added at the time that it was investigating the matter and cooperating with the police.

The latest models of the SU7 come with new door handles that can be opened without power.

Xiaomi has not responded to BBC requests for comment.

Tesla has also faced lawsuits in the US over its door handle designs.

The company has been sued by the only survivor of a crash in 2024 involving a Cybertruck - Tesla's electric pickup - that killed three college students in California.

Survivor Jordan Miller alleged that the Cybertruck's design trapped passengers in the burning vehicle and blocked their rescue.

The car did not have door handles and the electronic buttons meant to open the doors failed to work, according to his lawyers from The Veen Firm.

"When you design a vehicle with no mechanical way to open the doors from the outside, you are betting the electronics will work in every scenario, including a high-speed crash followed by a fire," said one of the lawyers in a statement.

In court filings, Tesla denied any wrongdoing and said the Cybertruck is compliant with US federal safety standards, the Guardian reported.

There have been other cases in the US of passengers, including children, allegedly being trapped in Tesla cars after the doors suddenly stopped working.

The BBC has contacted Tesla for comment.

What is being done about hidden handles?

In February, China said it would ban hidden door handles, making it the first country to do so.

The new rules, which take effect on 1 January 2027, mean new car designs without physical release mechanisms on the inside and outside of their doors cannot be sold.

The cars' interior must also carry signs to show how to open the door.

The measures in China come ahead of the US and European Union, which typically lead regulations around road safety and emissions, Dyer noted.

One reason is likely to be the sheer number of EVs in China, he added.

On 21 August, China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) announced that Tesla and some major Chinese car makers - including Xiaomi, XPeng and Geely - would recall more than four million vehicles.

The manufacturers were ordered to add warning labels inside vehicle doors to show passengers how to open them. Some cars will also get a software update that will lower their windows in the event of a crash.

Tesla, which started selling the Model S sedan with hidden door handles in China in 2014, is recalling nearly three million cars, according to the SAMR.

The agency said the recalled cars have door handles that are "difficult to identify" because they are a similar colour to the vehicle's interior trim.

In the event of an electrical failure, the handles' design may also prevent passengers from quickly opening the doors to escape or "hinder rescue efforts" by bystanders, the SAMR added.

Xiaomi, XPeng and Geely will also recall a total of more than 750,000 vehicles.

Some engineers say the measures may not go far enough to resolve safety concerns.

Engineering instructor Lim Hong Wee said the measures do not address the need for a mechanical way to open the doors.

Access to a car during an emergency should not depend on software, said Lim from the National University of Singapore.

The measures mainly address the issue of people being able to get out of a vehicle, but do not provide a reliable way for rescuers to get in, said Gokul Krithivasan from risk management consultancy SecureSafe.

Warning labels are also a "weak remedy", he added. "When panicked, people fall back on their instinctive responses, and don't read small print in a dark and possibly smoke-filled cabin."

For now, it is unclear whether there will be similar recalls outside China.

The BBC understands that carmakers have not yet notified authorities of any plans for a similar recall in the US.

The world's carmakers are struggling to compete with China

Elon Musk's stratospheric rise to trillionaire status - in charts

The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration told the BBC that it is reviewing whether it will require emergency door-exit systems in vehicles.

In Europe, regulators have flagged the potential hazards related to hidden handles and drafted new standards to ensure they still work even if a car's power is cut off.

Engineering lecturer Lyu Chen said that while concealed door handles are still common in EV designs, manufacturers and regulators are paying increasing attention to how they design their doors.

Since cars are built to sell globally, it is likely that the safety requirements in China will be adopted elsewhere, he added.

"The common principle is clear: emergency entry and exit should remain possible even after a loss of electrical power."

articles.title: Instagram chief testifies at Meta trial, says few teens used safety feature
articles.summary: Meta is on trial over claims it hooked young users on its platforms despite mental health risks.
articles.body:
The top executive at Instagram has admitted that few teenagers have used a feature meant to counter addiction before it was turned on by default, as hearings in a landmark trial against its parent company, Meta , continue in the United States.

Adam Mosseri testified on Tuesday as Meta’s trial – over accusations that it designed its platforms, including Facebook, to be addictive to young people – entered its second week.

list 2 of 3 Meta lawsuits: Is social media facing a global legal reckoning?

list 3 of 3 Landmark trial on Meta’s impact on children’s mental health begins in US

Mosseri, who has led Instagram since 2018, denied any suggestion by US states suing Meta that Instagram had stalled by not making the “Take a Break” feature the default setting for teenagers until September 2024, nearly three years after its launch.

“Most teens didn’t want it,” Mosseri said. “We decided to push forward with it anyway.”

Mosseri is a central witness in the lawsuit brought by 29 US states, in what experts call the biggest legal test yet of social media’s effects on young users.

Four of the states – California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey – have accused Meta of designing the platforms to hook young users, driving anxiety, depression and even suicide, while misleading consumers about the platforms’ safety.

All 29 states say Meta violated US federal law by improperly collecting and employing the personal data of children under 13 while they used its platforms.

The states are seeking approximately $200bn in damages from Meta.

Meta has rejected accusations that it sought to addict children, saying its research showed no clear link between adolescents’ social media use and a lack of wellbeing.

Under questioning from Jason Slothouber, a lawyer for Colorado, Mosseri acknowledged that the percentage of teenagers using Take a Break was in the low single digits before Instagram made it ⁠the default.

Take a Break encourages teenage users to close the app after a certain amount of time. Mosseri had estimated in a December 2021 blog post that more than 90 percent of teenagers who turned the feature on kept it on.

That number, however, referred to the number of those who had turned on the feature.

When asked whether Meta had disclosed its low adoption, which had reached only 1 or 2 percent of accounts, Mosseri admitted the company had not, but said the safety features were later turned on by default in Teen Accounts, which launched in 2024 and have parental controls.

Former Meta employees have said that features such as Take a Break and Quiet Mode were difficult to find and not widely used, casting doubt on whether they represented a serious effort by the company to limit screen time for young users .

“In my experience, Take a Break is a feature that’s designed to fail,” Arturo Bejar, a former Meta engineering director, testified last week.

George Volichenko, a data scientist who worked on safety features at Instagram in 2022 and 2023, likewise stated on Monday that adoption rates of such features were “very low” and that company leadership had declined to approve turning on Quiet Mode by default for young teenagers.

He added that turning on such features automatically would have had a “notable negative impact” on user engagement.

Jurors are expected to issue an advisory verdict. US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers will decide whether Meta is liable and, if so, determine any civil penalties and changes to Facebook and Instagram.

articles.title: Dozens killed in rebel attacks on Sudan’s Kordofan, medical group says
articles.summary: Sudan Doctors Network says SPLM-N rebels killed 27 people in South Kordofan, including four children.
articles.body:
A medical organisation has accused a Sudanese rebel group aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of killing 27 people, including four children, in the southern province of South Kordofan.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Sudan Doctors Network said the killings were carried out by the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas inhabited by the Otoro tribe in South Kordofan.

“The attacks resulted in a large wave of displacement among citizens towards the Abu Hitan area and Kadugli,” it said.

Targeting unarmed civilians on ethnic grounds constitutes a “clear violation of international humanitarian law”, the group added, warning that continued violations threatened to turn “the conflict in South Kordofan into a broader ethnic conflict”.

The killings follow intense fighting earlier this year between forces linked to SPLM-N and the Otoro tribe, which is a minority group in the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan.

The ethnic standoff, first instigated by land disputes, adds another layer to the country’s ongoing civil war , which broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese army and the RSF.

The Sudan Doctors Network urged the international community to exert pressure on SPLM-N leadership to halt attacks on civilians, noting that women were also among those wounded in the latest attacks.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the ruling party of neighbouring South Sudan.

Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

The civil war in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people and forced some 14 million people from their homes.

According to the World Health Organization, some 33.7 million people, or two-thirds of the country’s population, require humanitarian assistance.

The Sudan Doctors Network urged the international community to exert pressure on SPLM-N leadership to halt attacks on civilians, noting that women were also among those wounded in the latest attacks.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the ruling party of neighbouring South Sudan.

Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

The civil war in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people and forced some 14 million people from their homes.

According to the World Health Organization, some 33.7 million people, or two-thirds of the country's population, require humanitarian assistance.

articles.title: Chinese artist Gao Zhen sentenced to 3 years in prison over satirical Mao artworks
articles.summary: Gao Zhen, who is based in the U.S., was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024 and charged over works that authorities deemed insulting to revolutionary figures.
articles.body: BANGKOK — Chinese artist Gao Zhen was sentenced to three years in prison Tuesday for “infringing upon the reputation of heroes” through his satirical works of art, including statues of China’s former leader Mao Zedong. The U.S.-based Gao, who was part of an artistic duo known internationally as the Gao Brothers, was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024. He has been in official custody since then. He was sentenced by the Sanhei People’s Court in northern Hebei province, according to his wife, Zhao Yaliang. The charges against Gao relate to artistic works that China’s authorities deem insulting to revolutionary figures. One was a 2009 statue called “Mao’s Guilt,” which shows the former leader and founder of modern China kneeling in repentance, and another was the “Miss Mao” series of caricatures depicting Mao with breasts and an engorged nose. Shane Yi, a researcher at Chinese Human Rights Defenders, who has been advocating for Gao’s case, described the sentence as “a very clear case of a violation of a person’s freedom of expression.” Yi said the artist plans to appeal the sentence and noted that the artworks in question were created before the law Gao was sentenced with had been passed. The court did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Amnesty International criticized the court sentence, which it described as a deterrent against artistic expression. “The lengthy pretrial detention and, ultimately, decision to convict Gao Zhen and sentence him to the maximum three-year prison term under this offense illustrate the authorities’ determination to deter others from engaging in independent artistic expression,” said Amnesty’s China director, Sarah Brooks. “No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history,” she said. Zhao said she hopes to be reunited with her husband and be able to return to the U.S., where the family had immigrated. “I felt two years was my limit, and I was really disappointed and sad. I haven’t been able to catch my breath,” she said. She had prepared clothes for her husband hoping that he would be released. Chinese courts often count pretrial detention as time served in a sentence. The Gao Brothers, whose works addressed themes of authoritarianism and censorship, became famous in a time of relative openness in China and were exhibited both inside the country and abroad. However, in recent years, the state has increased its controlling grip on certain aspects of expression, especially in regard to political figures with the passage of the law in 2018 that bans criticism of the nation’s heroes.

articles.title: Chinese humanoid robot that beat Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint record does it again, but even faster
articles.summary: The race was part of the World Humanoid Robot Games, an Olympic-style competition in Beijing that showcases China’s rapid advances in robotics amid growing rivalry with the U.S.
articles.body: BEIJING — A Chinese humanoid robot set a new 100-meter sprint record of 8.86 seconds in Beijing on Tuesday, beating its robot competitors — and the fastest recorded human time. The race was part of China’s World Humanoid Robot Games, an Olympic-style competition now in its second year in Beijing. The event is also a showcase for China’s rapid advances in robotics amid an intensifying technology rivalry with the U.S. The Tiangong Ultra humanoid robot beat its own record of 9.39 seconds it had set just three days earlier at the event’s opening on Saturday. For comparison, the men’s 100-meter world record is 9.58 seconds, set by Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt in 2009. Experts are amazed to see such progress in the humanoid robot industry. “This is a significant milestone — not simply because the robot ran faster than a human, but because of what it takes to make a bipedal robot run at this speed,” said Dennis Hong, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at the University of California, Los Angeles. “As speed increases, balance, control, impacts, actuator performance and mechanical robustness all become much more challenging,” Hong said. The record-breaking robot fell after hitting the finish line, a padded barrier, with sparks flying from its waist. Hong pointed out that the fall leads to more meaningful and difficult questions: whether robots can move and stop safely, recognize unexpected obstacles, recover from mistakes and continue working, the capabilities that ultimately make them more useful. The games feature over 1,300 competitions involving more than 2,000 robots in 51 events like running, long jump and table tennis, as well as ballroom dancing. Unlike the traditional Olympics, the robots also compete in teams in real-world scenarios, including household tasks, hotel services and emergency response. “’Housekeeper’ and ‘caregiver’ robots are still in the pilot and validation phase,” China’s official newspaper People’s Daily said Monday, but “challenges are precisely where the focus of development lies. … China’s robotics industry is evolving toward higher quality and innovation.”

articles.title: Prosecutor in infamous killer mom case says women on Lindsay Clancy jury may bring ‘strange twist’ to verdict
articles.summary: Rep. Tommy Pope, who prosecuted Susan Smith, says women jurors may be less sympathetic to Lindsay Clancy's postpartum psychosis defense than expected.
articles.body: A South Carolina lawmaker who prosecuted Susan Smith in her infamous double-murder case says the women on Lindsay Clancy's jury could prove to be a "strange twist," and may be less sympathetic to her than many assume. Clancy, 36, has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder in connection with the deaths of her children — Cora, Dawson and Callan, all younger than 6 — who were discovered strangled at the family's home in January 2023. Her defense attorney says she was experiencing postpartum psychosis at the time she killed her children. LINDSAY CLANCY'S THREE CHILD VICTIMS FORGOTTEN AMID CROWDS OF SUPPORT: MOTHER OF SIX Testimony is expected to finish on Wednesday, with closing arguments anticipated for Thursday, after which the case will go to the jury. The panel seated for the trial is made up of 12 women and six men, but only 12 of them will deliberate, the rest serve as alternates and will be dismissed before deliberations begin. Smith is the South Carolina mother who was convicted of killing her two young sons, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander, by strapping them into her car and letting it roll into a lake. Prosecutors argued she killed them in part because the man she was romantically involved with didn't want a relationship with women who had kids. She was sentenced to life in prison. HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL Rep. Tommy Pope, who is currently the speaker pro tempore for the South Carolina House of Representatives, prosecuted Smith and told Fox News Digital that women on the jury might be less sympathetic to Clancy than people think. "For the most part, the women were the ones that said, you know, when I had my kids, I went through hell, or I went through depression, or I battled this, or I was overwhelmed. But they're the most important thing in my life," Pope said. "And so, strange twist, while a woman may have even faced postpartum depression, she may have overcome it and then be less sympathetic to Clancy." LINDSAY CLANCY TRIAL: POSTPARTUM IS REAL, BUT CHILD KILLING DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY, VETERAN PROSECUTOR SAYS On the flip side, Pope said Clancy's current physical condition might complicate things for the prosecution in an unexpected way. "A weird mix, too, is having her in the courtroom, whether she intentionally injured herself or, as the prosecution said, tried to slide down and just got injured. You have somebody that's now paralyzed, which obviously doesn't equate to killing three children," Pope said. "But some jurors, and I would think maybe even more so men, would think, well, she's already punished. She's in a wheelchair. So in a strange twist, it could almost be the opposite." LINDSAY CLANCY DEFENSE SCORES ‘EXTREMELY HELPFUL’ PSYCHOSIS CONCESSION AS EXPERT FLAGS NEXT HURDLE Prosecutors on Tuesday continued to challenge the psychosis argument that Clancy's defense attorney says frees her from criminal responsibility for her children's deaths. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Gregory Saathoff, a forensic psychiatrist at the University of Virginia who consults for the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, told jurors that Clancy's self-described auditory hallucinations were "very unusual." PROSECUTOR CORNERS LINDSAY CLANCY'S CATHOLIC MOTHER-IN-LAW WITH 'MORTAL SIN' QUESTION "What was significant to me is that she had not spoken about hearing voices before to any of the mental health professionals, psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, physicians and staff in the emergency department, or at McLean," Saathoff said. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS "This was the first time she reported that, and that she experienced an auditory hallucination, according to what she told me. So that was unusual. And then what was very unusual was the fact that the voice stopped with the strangling of her youngest son," he added. SEND US A TIP In another blow to Clancy's defense, prosecutors asked psychologist Kirk Heilbrun whether someone hearing a command hallucination could still conform their conduct to the law. WATCH: Prosecution expert says psychosis doesn't always erase knowing right from wrong GOT A TIP? "In some cases they can," he responded. LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS Earlier in the week, Clancy's defense called its own experts and argued she's not criminally responsible. Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist, testified that Clancy killed her children while she was experiencing a "command hallucination," stating she felt like "a puppet." It was almost like she was a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings," Resnick said. Outside the courtroom on Tuesday, one person told Fox News Digital she was there in support of Lindsay Clancy because "I've always been aware that mental health is something that's woefully in need of funding, education, all that." And...you know, we just had to figure it out ourselves. It shouldn't be that way. And I hope things change," the woman said.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella saw a record jump in his annual salary in 2025, a year later the signal from this annual package is clear, and it is that Microsoft Board thinks ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received a record total compensation package of about $96.5 million during fiscal year 2025. His latest pay package was up.
articles.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received a record total compensation package of about $96.5 million during fiscal year 2025. His latest pay package was up around 22% from $79.1 million a year earlier. The increase came as Microsoft reported higher revenue, operating income and cloud growth, with the companyâs board citing âexceptional progress in artificial intelligenceâ and saying Nadellaâs leadership had positioned Microsoft as a clear AI leader amid a generational technology shift.The structure of Nadellaâs pay package also mirrors the companyâs priorities. His 2025 package was worth more than $84 million in stock awards, $2.5 million base salary and $9.5 million in cash bonuses. More than 95% of his target annual compensation is performance-based, and at least 70% of that is equity-based.The package indicates that Microsoftâs board thinks artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud growth will remain central to the companyâs performance, with Nadellaâs compensation linked to metrics that include shareholder returns, revenue and cloud growth.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadellaâs compensation rises with AI and cloud growthMicrosoftâs revenue increased roughly 15% in fiscal 2025, and operating income was up 17%. Cloud revenue rose 23% to just under $169 billion while Azure revenue increased 34% to more than $75 billion.The companyâs proxy statement links Nadellaâs compensation to the broader business performance. His performance stock awards include long-term measures such as total shareholder return compared with the S&P 500, Microsoft incentive plan revenue, Azure and other cloud services revenue, and Microsoft Cloud revenue.Nadellaâs base salary is only a small part of the total package. Most of it comes in the form of equity awards, which rise and fall with Microsoftâs stock price, so much of his compensation is linked to the companyâs future performance.Microsoft board ties Nadellaâs pay to long-term performanceMicrosoft has also structured Nadellaâs compensation around longer performance periods rather than relying on time-based stock grants. The company uses overlapping performance periods, total shareholder return modifiers and multiyear vesting for his equity awards.That means a significant portion of Nadellaâs pay is tied to Microsoftâs performance over several years. It also ties his financial results to the same elements of the business central to Microsoftâs growth strategy, such as cloud services, Azure, AI performance, and shareholder returns.Nadellaâs pay also far outpaced the median employee pay at Microsoft, as the CEO-to-median-employee pay ratio hit almost 480-to-1 in 2025. So the size of the package has attracted attention, but the structure of the package is also important for understanding how the board has linked executive pay to company performance.Microsoftâs AI strategy reflected in CEO compensationMicrosoftâs 2025 results arrived as the company kept expanding its investments in artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure. The boardâs feedback focused on Nadella's progress on AI, even as the compensation plan continues to lean heavily on cloud and financial metrics.Nadellaâs compensation is heavily weighted to stock and performance, meaning his package is closely tied to Microsoftâs share price and business performance. âThe compensation structure is aligned with the boardâs view that AI and cloud services will be key to Microsoftâs performance going forward, while also aligning Nadellaâs financial outcome with those results.âGet the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: NHS failing child sex abuse victims, say psychiatrists
articles.summary: There have been decades of mistreatment and mismanagement of those who seek help later in life, say experts in a new, damning report.
articles.body:
People sexually abused as children who seek help in later life for mental health problems are being failed by the NHS, senior doctors have told the BBC.

The Royal College of Psychiatrists is issuing a public apology for what it says is decades of mismanagement and misdiagnosis in the UK.

For some, it has worsened their traumas, it said.

The college said mental health staff have been too focussed on treating symptoms rather than exploring how past traumatic experiences can still affect patients.

Support is improving, it said, but there must be better training and more investment - something NHS bosses have said is being introduced.

The apology has been included in a report by the college and given to the BBC.

Immediate past president of the college, Dr Lade Smith, said she was "sorry" that, too often, victims have suffered "avoidable harm when seeking help".

The report details how treatment has sometimes been inappropriate, while people have been re-traumatised by the experience of repeated assessments and history-taking and not always being believed.

Dr Smith told the BBC it was clear people were not getting the support they needed, and that this was not just a failing of psychiatrists, but the whole mental health system.

"Services are so fragmented. The system is set up to provide short, discreet episodes of care. Psychiatrists do not get the time to build up a relationship with patients so they can be properly supported.

"They are lucky if they get eight sessions of therapy, when it could take eight sessions for a person just to disclose the abuse.

"And these are just the people who get support – many don't even get seen by mental health services because services are so stretched," she said.

Estimates suggest nearly one in 10 adults in England and Wales were abused in childhood.

Such trauma increases the risk of mental health problems, including alcohol and drug misuse, eating disorders, self-harm, complex PTSD, anxiety and depression.

Many struggle to talk about the abuse. Around two-thirds of those abused as children have not disclosed it to services by the time they reach adulthood.

One in five never disclose, and many of those that do take decades to speak out.

Caroline Thompson, 65, is someone who feels let down by the NHS.

She was psychologically and sexually abused when she was a child.

She went on to raise a family and have a successful career as a specialist ear, nose and throat doctor.

It was not until she started experiencing terrifying nightmares, aged 55, that left her unable to function due to mental exhaustion and lack of sleep, that she realised she needed help and was referred to mental health services.

The psychiatrist she saw said her symptoms were unlikely to be due to the abuse because of the delay in presentation and given she had been able to have a family and successful career. She was diagnosed with anxiety and given anti-psychotic drugs.

"I had therapy for about a year and was then discharged. At that point I still didn't understand what was happening to me and I still couldn't function due to the nightmares and side-effects of the drugs. I had to give up the job I loved."

Caroline then got private therapy with a therapist who specialised in childhood trauma and gradually began to get better over the next few years.

She says: "It was astonishing to me that it was not understood that traumatic memories are buried in order for you to survive, and that those memories can surface years later. So any delay in presenting is quite normal."

The apology comes after the college set up a working group of experts, doctors and abuse survivors, including Caroline and chaired by leading consultant psychiatrists Jo Stubley and Maria Podlejska-Eyres, to review NHS care.

The group was set up after mental health services have seen a rise in people coming forward seeking help in the last decade or so, following high-profile abuse scandals involving schools, children's homes and religious institutions, as well as the Jimmy Savile crimes .

The college is calling for a number of changes. It is promising to develop specialist training materials for psychiatrists, but wants mandatory training for all mental health staff on the importance of trauma-informed care for survivors of child sex abuse.

And it has recommended national guidance be published on how to recognise and respond to disclosures of historic child sex abuse, as well as an overhaul of services so those needing help can get the long-term support they need.

Gabrielle Shaw, chief executive of the National Association for People Abused in Childhood, said this was a "significant and welcome" apology, but it must lead to "meaningful change".

"For too many adult survivors, mental health services have not felt like a route to safety or recovery."

A spokesman for NHS England said specialist services were available, highlighting how victims could access support 24 hours a day, seven days a week through sexual assault referral centres and counselling services with information about them available on the NHS website .

"People who have suffered historic child sexual abuse may not have spoken about it for years, so it's vital they know they can access specialist, trauma-informed support through the NHS," he added.

He also said steps were being taken to better support children and young people with additional training being provided to mental health support teams in schools and colleges.

If you've been affected by the issues in this story, you can find information, advice and support from the BBC's Action Line . Anyone feeling emotionally distressed or suicidal can call Samaritans for free on 116 123 or visit samaritans.org in the UK.

articles.title: Video from Colombia quake falsely linked to Peru tremor
articles.summary: After a 6.7-magnitude earthquake hit southern Peru on August 20, 2026, social media posts shared a video of a crumbling structure falsely claiming it shows v...
articles.body:
After a 6.7-magnitude earthquake hit southern Peru on August 20, 2026, social media posts shared a video of a crumbling structure falsely claiming it shows visuals from the tremor. The footage was in fact filmed in the Colombian city of Pereira after a 7.4-magnitude quake struck the country a week prior.

"Peru is in chaos. A powerful 7.2-magnitude earthquake has just struck the Ayacucho region in the south of the country," says a Chinese-language Douyin post shared on August 21, 2026.

The video shows the upper half of a blue building collapsing and debris falling as a man yells, "grandma, grandma...no...no" in Spanish.

A strong 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck southern Peru on August 20, US seismologists said, with authorities reporting minor injuries to three people, according to a preliminary report ( archived link ).

The Geophysical Institute of Peru (IGP) put the magnitude at 7.2 and said the quake occurred at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles).

In Peru, at least 22 homes, six schools and 12 medical centres have been impacted by the quake, the preliminary report found, as officials continue making damage assessments.

The tremor is the latest in a string of powerful quakes to strike South America, following deadly quakes in Venezuela on June 24 and Colombia on August 10 (archived here and here ).

Similar claims circulated across Weibo and Douyin and also spread in multiple languages such as Spanish and Japanese .

But the clip shows a quake in Colombia and not Peru.

A reverse image search on Google found an Instagram post that shared a similar photo showing the damaged blue building on August 13 ( archived link ). Its caption says Pereira.

A 7.4-magnitude tremor struck Colombia on August 10, the most powerful to hit the country in nearly half a century ( archived link ).

The quake killed nearly 300 people and destroyed more than 27,000 homes, with Pereira one of the cities affected the most ( archived link )

Google Maps street imagery of Carrera 7a in Pereira, Risaralda department, Colombia from March 2024 matches the scene in the false post ( archived link ).

Diaro del Otun, a media organisation based in Pereira, also published several photos of the same area on its Facebook account ( archived link ).

"Calle 32 at the junction of Carrera 6 and 9, Pereira...This is the state of these areas in central Pereira following the damage caused by the earthquake," the post's caption says.

AFP has debunked false claims related to recent quakes in South America.

articles.title: âSecure, predictable sea lanes indispensableâ: India urges UN to safeguard key maritime routes
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India has called on the international community to work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, saying se.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has called on the international community to work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, saying secure and predictable shipping routes are essential to ensure the uninterrupted movement of food, fertilisers, fuel and other vital commodities amid conflicts and growing disruptions to global supply chains.Speaking at a UN Security Council high-level open debate on Tuesday on the theme âFood Under Fire: The Security Council's Role in Mitigating Global and Local Food Crisesâ, Indiaâs Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said regional conflicts were increasingly producing consequences far beyond the immediate theatres of hostilities.âSecure and predictable maritime trade routes are indispensable for the uninterrupted movement of food, fertilisers, fuel and other essential commodities," Parvathaneni said, underscoring the need to preserve the safety and freedom of navigation for commercial shipping in accordance with international law.The call comes as conflicts and attacks on key maritime routes continue to threaten global food and energy supplies. UN secretary general Antonio Guterres told the Council that the Strait of Hormuz carries around a fifth of global oil supplies and a third of global fertiliser trade.âRestrictions and closures have driven up commodity prices and made availability plummet. And attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea are further threatening supply chains for food and other commodities,â Guterres said.Parvathaneni warned that disruptions to commercial shipping during conflicts could have cascading effects well beyond the affected region, with food-importing developing countries and humanitarian operations bearing a disproportionate burden.âThe international community must therefore work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, while ensuring that legitimate commercial trade and humanitarian shipments are able to proceed without undue impediment,â he said.India said the immediate priority for the Security Council should be to reduce the humanitarian consequences of conflicts by facilitating safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access, supporting de-confliction arrangements where appropriate and ensuring that Council measures, including sanctions regimes, do not inadvertently obstruct humanitarian assistance or legitimate food and agricultural trade.Parvathaneni also called for timely assessments of disruptions to critical supply chains covering food, fertiliser, fuel and humanitarian logistics, drawing on the expertise of the food and agriculture organisation, the World Food Programme and other relevant agencies.âSuch assessments must remain objective, evidence-based and free from politicisation,â he said.The envoy said food insecurity was fundamentally a consequence of conflict, political instability and underdevelopment, rather than their root cause. He called for greater cooperation among member states, international financial institutions, regional organisations and development partners to strengthen domestic agricultural production, diversify supply chains and improve storage and logistics infrastructure.âPredictable and affordable access to fertilisers, quality seeds, technology and concessional finance remains indispensable, particularly for developing countries. Open, transparent and rules-based trade in food and agricultural inputs also remains critical to global food security,â he said.India also cautioned against âover-reliance " on any single model of production, arguing that such dependence could leave food systems vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions, economic coercion and weaponisation.âWe must encourage small and marginal farmers to enhance their productivity and contribute to ensuring food security in developing countries of the Global South. We must also encourage climate-resilient crops such as millets rather than limit conceptions of food security to the biggest staple, grain crops such as rice, wheat and corn,â Parvathaneni said.Guterres said 2025 saw the highest number of armed conflicts since World War II alongside some of the highest levels of global acute hunger on record, with at least 266 million people facing acute food insecurity.He described the simultaneous confirmation of famine in Sudan and Gaza in 2025 as a âshameful milestoneâ, adding that conflict and violence were the primary drivers of hunger in 12 of the 13 hunger hotspots of greatest concern identified in the UNâs latest Hunger Hotspots report.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
